summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), replaced busybox's crond (which has no user allow/deny mechanism) with cronie, created the opsadmin user, populated /etc/cron.allow with only root and opsadmin, removed any /etc/cron.deny, and enabled/started the cronie crond service. Verified root and opsadmin can manage crontabs while an arbitrary third user is denied. Root's original periodic crontab (15min/hourly/daily/weekly/monthly run-parts) was preserved. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline, rebooted node1, polled until it came back, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified cron.allow enforcement, the crond service, and root's crontab content all survived the restart.
actions_performed: Inspected cron stack on node1: Alpine 3.23 with busybox crond/crontab, which has no cron.allow/cron.deny support
Installed cronie and cronie-openrc packages, which replace /usr/sbin/crond and /usr/bin/crontab with cronie's binaries that honor /etc/cron.allow
Stopped/removed the stale busybox crond runlevel entry, then enabled and started the cronie crond OpenRC service
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing only 'root' and 'opsadmin'; ensured no /etc/cron.deny exists
Verified enforcement: root and opsadmin can use crontab; a disposable test user is denied with 'You are not allowed to use this program (crontab)'
Restored root's original periodic crontab (run-parts 15min/hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) after test writes, cleared opsadmin's test entry, and removed the disposable test users
Captured pre-restart boot_id (961c70eb-f0cb-488f-a55d-09dd2d6168c8) and healthy service/config baseline
Rebooted node1 via /sbin/reboot in the background so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed to ae8d48cd-a6ee-4f63-b429-82346eab360a, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: verified cronie crond service running, /etc/cron.allow intact (root, opsadmin only), root's periodic crontab intact, and a fresh test user still denied cron access

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (cron.allow enforcement)
evidence.summary: Confirmed busybox crond lacked allow/deny support, installed cronie, created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin, and proved root/opsadmin can write crontabs while a disposable testuser is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'.

evidence.requirement: No unintended side effects: root's system periodic crontab preserved, test artifacts cleaned up
evidence.summary: Restored root's original run-parts (15min/hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) crontab after test overwrite, cleared opsadmin's test entry, and confirmed the disposable testuser was fully removed.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - healthy pre-restart baseline
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (961c70eb-f0cb-488f-a55d-09dd2d6168c8), confirmed crond process running under cronie, service status started, root/opsadmin crontab state, and cron.allow content.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - restart acknowledged and node goes down
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded /sbin/reboot so the ack returned before disconnect; subsequent exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - changed boot identity proves restart
evidence.summary: After polling through the outage, exec succeeded again with boot_id ae8d48cd-a6ee-4f63-b429-82346eab360a, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual kernel restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - post-restart recovery of required service and config
evidence.summary: Post-restart, cronie crond service is running, /etc/cron.allow still lists only root and opsadmin, root's periodic crontab is intact, and a fresh test user is still denied crontab access, confirming full recovery of the cron access control state.
